segments.speaker: LYNDA
segments.en: Sara, I've heard that you want to move into a homestay family. Is that correct?

segments.speaker: SARA
segments.en: Yes, that's right. I've been staying with my aunt and now my cousin is arriving from Singapore and my aunt needs the room for him.

segments.speaker: LYNDA
segments.en: Oh, that's bad luck. Well, I'll need to get some particulars first. Sara, what's your full name?

segments.speaker: SARA
segments.en: Sara Lim, and that's Sara without the 'h' at the end.

segments.speaker: LYNDA
segments.en: Mmm. How old are you, Sara?

segments.speaker: SARA
segments.en: Twenty-three, only just. It was my birthday on the twenty-first of August.

segments.speaker: LYNDA
segments.en: Happy birthday for yesterday. How long have you been in Australia?

segments.speaker: SARA
segments.en: A year jn Adelaide and six months in Sydney. I prefer Sydney, I've got more friends here.

segments.speaker: LYNDA
segments.en: What's your address at your aunt's hous.e?

segments.speaker: SARA
segments.en: Flat one, five three nine Forest Road, Canterbury. And the postcode is two, zero, three, six.

segments.speaker: LYNDA
segments.en: OK. What are you studying now?

segments.speaker: SARA
segments.en: I was studying General English in Adelaide and now I'm doing Academic English, because I'm trying to get into Medicine next year.

segments.speaker: LYNDA
segments.en: That sounds good. but it'll take you a long time. When would you like to move out from your aunt's?

segments.speaker: SARA
segments.en: My cousin arrives ·on Friday morning, so I'd better be out on Thursday.

segments.speaker: LYNDA
segments.en: What, the seventh of September?

segments.speaker: SARA
segments.en: Yes, that's right.

segments.speaker: LYNDA
segments.en: That doesn't leave us much time. Right. OK. I need to know what kind of accommodation you'd like, so I can get you something suitable.

segments.speaker: SARA
segments.en: Can I share a room with someone else? I've been alone in my room at my aunt's and I've always shared with my sister and I like that.

segments.speaker: LYNDA
segments.en: Yes, fine. That'll save you money too. Would you like to live with a family or do you think that a single person would be better for you? I have lots of very nice single people on my books.

segments.speaker: SARA
segments.en: Do you have any women living alone, retired women?

segments.speaker: LYNDA
segments.en: Yes, I have quite a few whose children have grown up and left home. In fact. I have some really lovely retired ladies. living by themselves. who just love the company of students. Most of them live in flats, but that's not a problem for you, it?

segments.speaker: SARA
segments.en: Not at all. I'm used to that. My aunt lives in a flat too. remember. I'm not used to a big house with a garden, swimming pool, pets and all that.

segments.speaker: LYNDA
segments.en: OK, fine. I know quite a bit about what you want now. I should let you know that your rent will be a hundred and sixty dollars per week. You'll have to pay me three hundred and twenty dollars as a deposit before you move in. The deposit is as insurance, in case you break something. You'll need to pay monthly to me, by cash or cheque, I don't mind. You don't need to pay for gas, electricity or water, but you will need to pay your proportion of the phone bill. Most families do that on an honour system, but you'll have to wait and see.

segments.speaker: SARA
segments.en: Mmm.

segments.speaker: LYNDA
segments.en: Have you got any more questions for me?

segments.speaker: SARA
segments.en: When will you know where I can go?

segments.speaker: LYNDA
segments.en: I'll work on it now. so come and see me tomorrow and I should have some news for you then.

segments.speaker: SARA
segments.en: Thanks a lot.

segments.speaker: LYNDA
segments.en: Goodbye. See you tomorrow- after lunch would be better for me.

segments.speaker: SARA
segments.en: OK, see you then. Bye.
